Vettel made his Ferrari debut by finishing third in the [Australian Grand Prix](/wiki/2015_Australian_Grand_Prix "2015 Australian Grand Prix").[[111]](#cite_note-112) He followed that up with winning the [Malaysian Grand Prix](/wiki/2015_Malaysian_Grand_Prix "2015 Malaysian Grand Prix"),[[112]](#cite_note-113) his first race victory for over a year and the first win for Ferrari for almost two years. After the race, an emotional Vettel paid tribute to Schumacher, saying that his hero's achievements with Ferrari made the first win all the more special.[[113]](#cite_note-114)

He won the [Hungarian Grand Prix](/wiki/2015_Hungarian_Grand_Prix "2015 Hungarian Grand Prix") to remain a championship contender after he started from third on the grid. He dedicated his victory to the driver [Jules Bianchi](/wiki/Jules_Bianchi "Jules Bianchi"), who died the week prior from injuries sustained in 2014.[[114]](#cite_note-115) At the halfway point of the season, Vettel was 42 points behind championship leader and [Mercedes](/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_in_Formula_One "Mercedes-Benz in Formula One") driver Hamilton.[[115]](#cite_note-116) Vettel was in third place in [Belgium](/wiki/2015_Belgian_Grand_Prix "2015 Belgian Grand Prix") when his right rear blew at high speed on the penultimate lap, likely ending any title chances given Hamilton's win. After the race, he ranted about the 'unacceptable' and 'unsafe' Pirelli tyres that could have caused him serious injury.[[116]](#cite_note-117)

fanoutqa_010650.x:
2019–20 Los Angeles Lakers season :: Playoffs :: Playoff notes :: chunk_0020
In the [NBA playoffs](/wiki/2020_NBA_playoffs "2020 NBA playoffs"), the Lakers faced off against the eight-seed [Portland Trail Blazers](/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_Portland_Trail_Blazers_season "2019–20 Portland Trail Blazers season") in the first round and won the series in five games. In the Western Conference Semifinals, they faced the fourth-seeded [Houston Rockets](/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_Houston_Rockets_season "2019–20 Houston Rockets season"), again winning in five games. The Lakers advanced to the Western Conference Finals for the first time since [2010](/wiki/2010_NBA_playoffs "2010 NBA playoffs"), where they defeated the [Denver Nuggets](/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_Denver_Nuggets_season "2019–20 Denver Nuggets season") in five games.

The Lakers reached the [NBA Finals](/wiki/2020_NBA_Finals "2020 NBA Finals") for the first time in a [decade](/wiki/2010_NBA_Finals "2010 NBA Finals"). In the Finals, the Lakers competed against the Eastern Conference champion [Miami Heat](/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_Miami_Heat_season "2019–20 Miami Heat season"); this was the first time that the two teams had met in the NBA Finals. The Lakers won the series in six games, winning the championship for the first time since the [2010 season](/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Los_Angeles_Lakers_season "2009–10 Los Angeles Lakers season"). They became the first team since the [2007–08 Boston Celtics](/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_Boston_Celtics_season "2007–08 Boston Celtics season") to miss the playoffs one season and win a championship the following season. The Lakers also tied the Celtics for the highest-ever number of NBA championship wins with 17.[[49]](#cite_note-49)[[5]](#cite_note-mcmenamin_10112020-5) The Lakers' [LeBron James](/wiki/LeBron_James "LeBron James") was named the [NBA Finals Most Valuable Player](/wiki/NBA_Finals_Most_Valuable_Player_Award "NBA Finals Most Valuable Player Award") (MVP) for the fourth time in his career. Rosalind Brewer :: Career :: Walgreens Boots Alliance (2021-2023) :: chunk_0004
On March 15, 2021, Rosalind Brewer was appointed as the CEO of [Walgreens Boots Alliance](/wiki/Walgreens_Boots_Alliance "Walgreens Boots Alliance"). Brewer became the only black woman to lead a [Fortune 500 company](/wiki/Fortune_500 "Fortune 500") during that timeframe.[[26]](#cite_note-26)[[27]](#cite_note-:5-27)

In 2023, Brewer's total compensation from Walgreens Boots Alliance was $14.1 million, or 407 times the median employee pay at Walgreens Boots Alliance for that year.[[28]](#cite_note-28)

In September 2023, Brewer agreed to step down as CEO in September 2023 after being in the role for two years.[[1]](#cite_note-Kavilanz-1) Under Brewer's tenure as CEO, the company's stock declined 47%.[[29]](#cite_note-29)

Brewer was a member of the board of directors at [Amazon](/wiki/Amazon_(company) "Amazon (company)") from 2019 to 2021.[[12]](#cite_note-:9-12)[[30]](#cite_note-30) She was a director of [Lockheed Martin](/wiki/Lockheed_Martin "Lockheed Martin") from 2011 to 2017, and [Molson Coors Brewing Company](/wiki/Molson_Coors_Brewing_Company "Molson Coors Brewing Company") from 2006 to 2011.[[11]](#cite_note-:3-11)[[13]](#cite_note-:10-13)[[31]](#cite_note-31)[[32]](#cite_note-32)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/84/HFe_H2_dppe_2.svg/250px-HFe_H2_dppe_2.svg.png)](/wiki/File:HFe_H2_dppe_2.svg)

A [dihydrogen complex](/wiki/Dihydrogen_complex "Dihydrogen complex") of iron, [HFe(H2)(dppe)2]+

H2 is relatively unreactive. The thermodynamic basis of this low reactivity is the very strong H–H bond, with a [bond dissociation energy](/wiki/Bond_dissociation_energy "Bond dissociation energy") of 435.7 [kJ/mol](/wiki/Joule_per_mole "Joule per mole").[[82]](#cite_note-82) It does form coordination complexes called [dihydrogen complexes](/wiki/Dihydrogen_complex "Dihydrogen complex"). These species provide insights into the early steps in the interactions of hydrogen with metal catalysts. According to [neutron diffraction](/wiki/Neutron_diffraction "Neutron diffraction"), the metal and two H atoms form a triangle in these complexes. The H-H bond remains intact but is elongated. They are acidic.[[83]](#cite_note-83)

Although exotic on Earth, the H+3 ion is common in the universe. It is a triangular species, like the aforementioned dihydrogen complexes. It is known as [protonated molecular hydrogen](/wiki/Trihydrogen_cation "Trihydrogen cation") or the trihydrogen cation.[[84]](#cite_note-Carrington-84)

Hydrogen reacts with [chlorine](/wiki/Chlorine "Chlorine") to produce [HCl](/wiki/HCl "HCl"), and with [bromine](/wiki/Bromine "Bromine") to produce [HBr](/wiki/Hydrogen_bromide "Hydrogen bromide"), via a [chain reaction](/wiki/Chain_reaction "Chain reaction"). The reaction requires initiation. For example, in the case of Br2, the dibromine molecule is split apart: Br2 + (UV light) → 2Br•. Propagating reactions consume hydrogen molecules and produce HBr, as well as Br and H atoms:

Br• + H2 → HBr + H

H + Br2 → HBr +Br

Finally the terminating reaction:

H + HBr → H2 + Br•

2 Br• → Br2

consumes the remaining atoms.[[85]](#cite_note-85): 289

fanoutqa_006298.x:

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/88/Virginia_Thomas.JPG)](/wiki/File:Virginia_Thomas.JPG)

Thomas was sworn in as a member of the U.S. Supreme Court by Justice [Byron White](/wiki/Byron_White "Byron White") on October 23, 1991. His wife, [Virginia Thomas](/wiki/Virginia_Thomas "Virginia Thomas"), looks on in the foreground.

On October 15, 1991, the Senate voted to confirm Thomas as an [associate justice](/wiki/Associate_Justice_of_the_Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States "Associate Justice of the Supreme Court of the United States"), 52–48.[[142]](#cite_note-CRS-R44234-144)[[177]](#cite_note-179) Thomas received the votes of 41 Republicans and 11 Democrats, while 46 Democrats and two Republicans voted to reject his nomination.[[178]](#cite_note-NYT19911016-180) As of 2024, Thomas is the most recent Supreme Court justice to be confirmed by a Senate controlled by the opposing party of the appointing president.

The 99 days during which Thomas's nomination was pending in the Senate was the second-longest of the 16 nominees receiving a final vote since 1975, second only to Bork's 108 days.[[142]](#cite_note-CRS-R44234-144) The vote to confirm Thomas was the narrowest margin for approval in more than 100 years.[[179]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZepposHall1992871-181)

Thomas received his [commission](/wiki/Commission_(document) "Commission (document)") on October 23 and took the prescribed constitutional and judicial oaths of office, becoming the Court's [106th justice](/wiki/List_of_justices_of_the_Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States "List of justices of the Supreme Court of the United States").[[180]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZepposHall1992870-182)[[c]](#cite_note-184) He was sworn in by Justice [Byron White](/wiki/Byron_White "Byron White") in a ceremony initially scheduled for October 21, which was postponed because of the death of Chief Justice [William Rehnquist](/wiki/William_Rehnquist

Mercury (planet) :: part 03 :: chunk_0002
**Mercury** is the first [planet](/wiki/Planet "Planet") from the [Sun](/wiki/Sun "Sun") and the [smallest in the Solar System](/wiki/List_of_Solar_System_objects_by_size "List of Solar System objects by size"). It is a [rocky planet](/wiki/Rocky_planet "Rocky planet") with a [trace atmosphere](/wiki/Atmosphere_of_Mercury "Atmosphere of Mercury") and a surface [gravity](/wiki/Gravity "Gravity") slightly higher than that of [Mars](/wiki/Mars "Mars"). The surface of Mercury is similar to Earth's [Moon](/wiki/Moon "Moon"), being [cratered](/wiki/Impact_crater "Impact crater"), with an expansive [rupes](/wiki/Rupes "Rupes") system generated from [thrust faults](/wiki/Thrust_fault "Thrust fault"), and bright [ray systems](/wiki/Ray_system "Ray system"), formed by [ejecta](/wiki/Ejecta "Ejecta"). Its largest crater, [Caloris Planitia](/wiki/Caloris_Planitia "Caloris Planitia"), has a diameter of 1,550 km (960 mi), which is about one-third the diameter of the planet (4,880 km or 3,030 mi). Being the most [inferior](/wiki/Inferior_planet "Inferior planet") orbiting planet, it always appears close to the Sun in [Earth](/wiki/Earth "Earth")'s sky, either as a "morning star" or an "evening star". It is the planet with the highest [delta-v](/wiki/Delta-v "Delta-v") required for travel from Earth, as well as to and from the [other planets](/wiki/List_of_planets_in_the_Solar_System "List of planets in the Solar System") in the [Solar System](/wiki/Solar_System "Solar System").

fanoutqa_009626.t: QS World University Rankings :: Rankings :: QS World University Rankings :: Employer reputation :: chunk_0004
fanoutqa_009626.x:
QS World University Rankings :: Rankings :: QS World University Rankings :: Employer reputation :: chunk_0004
QS's Employer Reputation indicator is obtained using another survey, like Academic Reputation, and accounts for 15% of an institution's overall score. The most recent edition surveyed some 99,000 employers at companies and organisations that hire graduates on a significant or global scale.

This survey was introduced in 2005 in the belief that employers track graduate quality, making this a barometer of teaching quality and the level of work readiness acquired by students, a famously problematic factor to measure. University standing here is of special interest to potential students, and acknowledging this was the impetus behind the inaugural QS Graduate Employability Rankings, published in November 2015.[[19]](#cite_note-britannia-study-19)[[25]](#cite_note-25) However, these rankings were subsequently discontinued in 2021, with its data rolled into the QS World University Rankings methodology.

The first description of phenylalanine was made in 1879, when [Schulze](/wiki/Ernst_Schulze_(chemist) "Ernst Schulze (chemist)") and Barbieri identified a compound with the [empirical formula](/wiki/Empirical_formula "Empirical formula"), C9H11NO2, in [yellow lupine](/wiki/Lupinus_luteus "Lupinus luteus") (*Lupinus luteus*) seedlings. In 1882, [Erlenmeyer](/wiki/Emil_Erlenmeyer "Emil Erlenmeyer") and Lipp first synthesized phenylalanine from [phenylacetaldehyde](/wiki/Phenylacetaldehyde "Phenylacetaldehyde"), [hydrogen cyanide](/wiki/Hydrogen_cyanide "Hydrogen cyanide"), and [ammonia](/wiki/Ammonia "Ammonia").[[5]](#cite_note-5)[[6]](#cite_note-6)

The genetic [codon](/wiki/Codon "Codon") for phenylalanine was first discovered by [J. Heinrich Matthaei](/wiki/J._Heinrich_Matthaei "J. Heinrich Matthaei") and [Marshall W. Nirenberg](/wiki/Marshall_W._Nirenberg "Marshall W. Nirenberg") in 1961. They showed that by using [mRNA](/wiki/Messenger_RNA "Messenger RNA") to insert multiple [uracil](/wiki/Uracil "Uracil") repeats into the [genome](/wiki/Genome "Genome") of the [bacterium](/wiki/Bacterium "Bacterium") *[E. coli](/wiki/Escherichia_coli "Escherichia coli")*, they could cause the bacterium to produce a [polypeptide](/wiki/Peptide "Peptide") consisting solely of repeated phenylalanine amino acids. This discovery helped to establish the nature of the [coding](/wiki/Coding_strand "Coding strand") relationship that links information stored in [genomic](/wiki/Genome "Genome") nucleic acid with [protein expression](/wiki/Proteome "Proteome") in the living cell.

Closeup of a Shiba Inu

A study in Japan on [patella luxation](/wiki/Patella_luxation "Patella luxation") in small breeds found the Shiba Inu to have the second highest rate of the condition, with 35% of the Shiba Inus surveyed being affected.[[28]](#cite_note-28) Three genes belonging to the breed were associated with [glaucoma](/wiki/Glaucoma "Glaucoma"), as found in an analysis of [DNA sequencing](/wiki/DNA_sequencing "DNA sequencing").[[29]](#cite_note-29) Another study from Japan reviewing cases of dogs presented for [ophthalmologic](/wiki/Ophthalmologic "Ophthalmologic") examination found the Shiba Inu to make up 33% of all glaucoma cases whilst only making up 2.7% of the total population used in the study.[[30]](#cite_note-30) [Pyometra](/wiki/Pyometra "Pyometra"), a uterine infection of intact bitches, is slightly more common in the Shiba Inu.[[31]](#cite_note-31)[[32]](#cite_note-32) The Shiba Inu is predisposed to [canine atopic dermatitis](/wiki/Dog_skin_disorders "Dog skin disorders").[[33]](#cite_note-33)[[34]](#cite_note-34)[[35]](#cite_note-35) An auto-immune disease common in Akitas [Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada-like syndrome](/wiki/Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada-like_syndrome "Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada-like syndrome") is known to occur in the Shiba Inu.[[36]](#cite_note-36)

A review of cemetery data in Japan found that the Shiba Inu had a life expectancy of 15.5 years,[[37]](#cite_note-37) greater than any other breed. A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 14.6 years for the breed compared to an average of 12.7 for purebreeds and 12 for [crossbreeds](/wiki/Mongrel "Mongrel").[[38]](#cite_note-38)

From the beginning of the nineteenth century, [bulldogs](/wiki/Bulldog "Bulldog") were bred in the United Kingdom for purposes other than traditional [blood sports](/wiki/Blood_sports "Blood sports") such as bull-baiting, which were banned in 1835.[[5]](#cite_note-coile-5): 5 By the middle of the century there were miniature bulldogs, most weighing around 7–11 kg (15–24 lb).[[5]](#cite_note-coile-5): 6

At the same time, [lace](/wiki/Lace "Lace") workers from [Nottingham](/wiki/Nottingham "Nottingham") who were displaced by the [Industrial Revolution](/wiki/Industrial_Revolution "Industrial Revolution") began to settle in [Normandy](/wiki/Normandy "Normandy"), France.[[6]](#cite_note-leighton-6): 58 They brought a variety of dogs with them, including Toy Bulldogs.[[7]](#cite_note-Get_to_Know_the_French_Bulldog-7) The dogs became popular in France and a trade in imported small Bulldogs was created, with breeders in England sending over Bulldogs that they considered to be too small, or with faults such as ears that stood up. By 1860, there were few Toy Bulldogs left in England, such was their popularity in France.[[5]](#cite_note-coile-5): 6

The small Bulldog type gradually became thought of as a breed, and received a name, the Bouledogue Français.[[5]](#cite_note-coile-5): 6 This French version of the English name is also a contraction of the words *boule* ('ball') and *dogue* ('mastiff'). The family attended an [Assembly of God](/wiki/Assembly_of_God "Assembly of God") church, where he found his initial musical inspiration.[[11]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGuralnick199412–14-13) Vernon moved from one [odd job](/wiki/Handyman "Handyman") to the next,[[12]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGuralnick199411–12,_23–24-14)[[13]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEVictor2008419-15) and the family often relied on neighbors and government food assistance.
